newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LUTON REVIVE MEMORIES OF 1988 WITH LEAGUE CUP UPSET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LUTON REVIVE MEMORIES OF 1988 WITH LEAGUE CUP UPSET.

text.p: Luton, who have dropped two divisions since winning the English League Cup in 1988, revived old memories of cup campaigns when they knocked premier league Derby out of the competition 3-2 on aggregate on Wednesday.

Luton, who won the first leg of the second round tie 1-0 at home last week, forced a 2-2 draw at Derby who hit back after a 12th minute Kim Grant goal with goals from Dean Sturridge after 40 minutes and Paul Simpson five minutes later.
But Thony Thorpe scored Luton's equaliser midway through the second half and that was enough to put them into the third round.
Second division Blackpool, thumped 4-1 at home by Chelsea last week, beat Ruud Gullit's team 3-1 at Stamford Bridge but narrowly went out 5-4 on aggregate.
But the other premier league sides playing against lower division opposition had no problems.

Injury-hit Tottenham briefly put their league worries behind them with a 3-0 win over second division with 18-year-old rookie Rory Allen scoring twice in the second half for a 4-1 aggregate victory. Darren Anderton, who scored in the 1-1 draw at Preston last week, opened the scoring for Tottenham after 31 minutes.

Tottenham, who have not won a league match at home since March were boosted by the return from injury of England striker Teddy Sheringham after five matches, but Anderton's bad luck with injuries continued and he was substituted in the second half.

Southampton, without a win in the premier league after seven matches, thumped Peterborough 4-1 for a 6-1 aggregate victory, while Leicester beat third division Scarborough 2-1 with a 90th minute Garry Parker penalty giving Leicester victory on the night and a 4-1 aggregate win.

In other matches Wimbledon drew 1-1 at first division Portsmouth to go through 2-1 on aggregate and West Ham were made to work hard for a 1-0 win over third division Barnet for a 2-1 aggregate success.
Croatian midfielder Slaven Bilic scored his first goal for the Hammers after 48 minutes to spare his side's blushes.
